_comment: Human-readable semantics for harness-based errors -- boolean flags the SEED workflow (projects/travel_mas_refactored/seed/mas_workflow.py) sets on AgentOutput.metadata when a case crashes outright (no plan produced at all), tallied into project_metrics['harness_checks'] by this project's scorer (see aggregate() in adapter/scorer_impl.py). Unlike error_semantics.json's task checks (which come from the immutable scorer and never change), these flag NAMES are defined by the seed's own mutable workflow code -- this file describes the flags as they exist in the CURRENT seed specifically. If the seed workflow is deliberately edited to add/rename/remove a flag, update this file to match; a flag not covered here simply falls back to Curriculum's generic explanation rather than breaking anything.
sightseeing_failed: Fires when the sightseeing stage never produced a usable itinerary at all, even after its own retry -- there was no real day-by-day plan to hand to the rest of the pipeline, so the whole case ends with an empty result instead of a scored plan.
budget_exhausted: Fires only when one of the flight, train, or sightseeing stages genuinely used up its entire tool-calling budget (hit its iteration cap) without finishing on its own -- the stage was cut off mid-task rather than reaching a natural stopping point. This is never set just because the stage's output ended up unusable for some other reason -- see task_failure for that.
task_failure: Fires when the sightseeing stage failed to produce a usable itinerary for a reason OTHER than running out of iteration budget -- e.g. its final wrap-up retry (which has no iteration limit of its own) still did not produce a valid output tag. task_failure_reason carries the actual failure text (e.g. the model's raw wrap-up response) so the specific cause doesn't have to be guessed at.
output_truncated: Fires when the agent's output was truncated -- an LLM call was cut off by its own output token limit before it finished responding, unrelated to budget_exhausted (which is about running out of tool-calling turns, not output length).
